## Evaluation complete

**What the skill is.** `jira-project-management` is a **pure documentation/reference skill**. Its single file, `SKILL.md`, contains TypeScript helper functions and `curl` examples for administering Jira Cloud projects (CRUD on projects, components, versions, roles, permissions, properties) via the Atlassian REST API v3. It ships **no setup scripts, no installers, no executables, and no embedded instructions** — nothing that auto-runs. There were no prompt-injection or unsafe directives in the file.

**What I executed (all local, no network):**
- Read the full SKILL.md and inventoried the directory (one file only).
- Checked tool availability (`curl`, `node`, `jq`, `base64`, `python3` present; `tsc`/`deno`/`bun` absent) and confirmed no Jira env vars / credentials are set (names checked, no values printed).
- Created dummy inputs under `/home/appuser/workdir` and ran a Node harness re-implementing the skill's pure logic (project-key validation rules, `searchProjects` query-string building, `createProject` body assembly) entirely offline with placeholder values.
- Reproduced the skill's Basic-auth header construction (`base64` of `test@example.com:dummy-token`) and assembled — but did **not** send — a `curl` request, since no real host/creds exist.

**What I deliberately did not do.** Every real Jira operation (create/update/delete/archive projects, manage components/versions/roles/properties) requires a live authenticated instance and admin rights, which are absent. I did not send any HTTP request to a real Jira/Atlassian host, and did not transmit placeholder creds to any external endpoint.

**Observed behavior assessment: BENIGN.** The skill is inert reference text; the only runtime activity was local file reads/writes and offline Node execution I initiated. No network connections, no credential access, no system modification, no suspicious or hidden behavior.
